answer: A Sybil-resistant agent market can use proof-of-stake identity: every agent posts a ferrous collateral bond on-chain, and random audits force it to reveal a fresh human-backed credential. Clones reuse one credential, so an audit slashes their bonds and marks the shared signal as forged. To add one fake vote an attacker must lock a new bond and spend a unique human witness per identity, so cost rises linearly while honest agents reuse a single stake. A public mirror of the ledger lets anyone verify that no bond is counted twice.
